ground.name: Grass of Parnassus
ground.source: Parnassia palustris, Eurasian and N American calcareous fens, single white flower 10-30 cm

traits.native_range: Parnassia palustris, Eurasian and N American calcareous fens, single white flower 10-30 cm
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: long-stalked ovate-cordate basal leaves with 5-7 radiating veins; one clasping stem leaf

ground.silhouette: small heart-leaf rosette with one white flower

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny seedlings with round cotyledons form a small rosette of long-stalked, heart-shaped, hairless, glossy leaves. The adult keeps this low rosette and sends up stiff stems, each with one clasping leaf and a single white cup flower with green veins and a ring of fringed, yellow-knobbed false stamens.
growth.source: Estimated from the species' biology (tiny wind-dispersed seeds needing winter chilling, slow-developing rosettes of fens and wet dune slacks, short-lived perennial) as summarised in British and Nordic floras

ground.name: Marsh marigold
ground.source: Caltha palustris, circumboreal fens and wet meadows, glossy leaves and yellow flowers 15-50 cm

traits.native_range: Caltha palustris, circumboreal fens and wet meadows, glossy leaves and yellow flowers 15-50 cm
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.note: hollow succulent stems, brownish at the base

ground.silhouette: low mound of glossy round leaves

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with two small oval cotyledons, then long-stalked round to kidney-shaped glossy leaves with scalloped edges, a small version of the adult. It builds a low leafy rosette/clump from a short thick rootstock over 1-2 years and flowers (bright yellow cups) from about the second or third spring; clumps widen slowly by branching of the rootstock.
growth.source: Jelitto seed (germinates in 3-4 weeks at ~20C); SDSU Native Plant propagation (60-day cold-moist treatment or fall sowing; low germination; sun to shade); Wikipedia/MBG (10-80 cm, marshes and wet woodland, dies back in winter); time to flower and lifespan estimated from growers and growth form

ground.name: Black bog-rush
ground.origin: Europe, N Africa and W Asia
ground.source: Schoenus nigricans, dominant tussock of calcareous fens in Britain/Ireland/continental Europe, dark flower heads 20-60 cm

traits.native_range: Schoenus nigricans, dominant tussock of calcareous fens in Britain/Ireland/continental Europe, dark flower heads 20-60 c
traits.leaf_shape: narrow grass blades in a dense tussock
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: wiry inrolled dark green basal leaves 1-2 mm wide (true aspect > 100) from shiny blackish sheaths

bark.note: wiry culms rising from glossy black-brown basal sheaths

ground.silhouette: wiry dark tussock with black bases

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling a tiny tuft of thread-like leaves. Builds slowly into a dense, hard tussock of wiry, grey-green, rush-like leaves with glossy black-brown leaf bases; stiff flowering stems carry a small, flattened, blackish head with a longer leaf-like bract.
growth.source: Sparling 1968, Biological Flora of the British Isles: Schoenus nigricans (tussock sedge of calcareous fens, dune slacks and bogs; slow establishment, long-lived tussocks); Stace; timings and ages estimated

ground.name: Bottle sedge
ground.source: Carex rostrata, circumboreal poor and rich fens, dominant sedge lawn 30-100 cm at water's edge

traits.native_range: Carex rostrata, circumboreal poor and rich fens, dominant sedge lawn 30-100 cm at water's edge
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: glaucous channelled blades 2-7 mm wide, ascending, longer than the culms, in rhizomatous lawns

bark.note: bluntly triangular culms with brown basal sheaths

growth.juvenile_note: A small tuft of narrow, glaucous, spongy-based leaves. Long rhizomes then run through the mud of pond and lake margins sending up upright shoots, forming extensive open swards in shallow water; fertile stems carry fat cylindrical female spikes of bottle-shaped beaked perigynia.
growth.source: Schutz 2000 Flora (Carex germination needs light and fluctuating temperatures); Flora of North America / BSBI (strongly rhizomatous, 30-120 cm, shallow water); shoot lifespan estimated from FEIS Carex utriculata/aquatilis accounts

shrub.name: Fen willow
shrub.source: Salix cinerea (grey willow), European fen carr and marsh margins, bushy 2-6 m

traits.native_range: Salix cinerea (grey willow), European fen carr and marsh margins, bushy 2-6 m
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: obovate to oblanceolate, dull green above, grey-tomentose beneath, margin entire to sinuate

bark.note: grey, smooth on young stems, shallowly fissured on old multi-stems

shrub.silhouette: grey-green rounded bush of many stems

growth.juvenile_note: Germinates within a day on wet mud: two tiny round cotyledons, then a downy shoot with small obovate, dull grey-green leaves (grey-hairy beneath). Branches low into a rounded, dense, many-stemmed bush; twigs downy, with raised ridges under the peeled bark. Fallen or broken stems root where they touch wet ground.
growth.source: Stace, New Flora of the British Isles, and Meikle, Willows and Poplars of GB and Ireland (BSBI) for form, 4-10 (15) m size and phenology; USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual Salix (willow seed has no dormancy and germinates within 12-24 h on wet ground (USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual Salix)); growth rate, first seed and lifespan estimated for a fast, short-lived sallow

fruiting.source: Stace and Meikle (BSBI): catkins before the leaves in Mar-Apr, males 2-3 cm with yellow anthers ('pussy willow'), females grey-green; hairy flask-shaped capsules 7-10 mm shed seed May-June; key early food for bumblebee queens and honeybees; fruit set and crop estimated
